transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

I keep starting school projects and committee work with good intentions, but I can’t seem to follow through and finish things on time, no matter how hard I try to stay on top of it. I'm a secondary school teacher, and after a tough mid-year performance review, my department head and my wife strongly urged me to seek an evaluation. It's just getting really frustrating because I want to do well, but I'm falling behind.
Have you had these problems with staying organized, finishing tasks, or paying attention since childhood or your teen years, or did they start only more recently?

These issues actually go all the way back to my childhood; even in primary school, my report cards always said I was bright but constantly daydreamed and lost my homework. While things have really come to a head over the last 11 months with my new teaching responsibilities, I've struggled with this throughout university and my entire career.

Do these attention and organization problems happen in more than one part of your life, like both at work and at home, and can you give one example from home? Have they caused ongoing problems in your relationships or daily responsibilities outside of work too?

Yes, they definitely affect my home life too. I've missed dentist appointments and paid bills late because they just slip my mind, and my wife gets very frustrated because I'm constantly misplacing things around the house and working late into the evening to catch up instead of spending time with her.

Besides the attention and organization problems, do you also often feel restless or fidgety, talk a lot, interrupt others, or act before thinking? Or has it mainly been trouble with focus, forgetfulness, and finishing tasks?

It has definitely been mainly trouble with focus, forgetfulness, and finishing tasks. I don't really feel fidgety, hyperactive, or prone to interrupting others at all. My main issue is just that my mind constantly drifts off, I lose track of things, and I struggle to follow through on my projects.

When your focus gets worse, is it mainly only during times when you’re feeling depressed, very anxious, or unusually stressed, or is it present even when your mood is otherwise okay? Have you had any long periods of low mood or excessive anxiety that seemed to drive these problems?

These focus problems are present even when my mood is completely fine, and they aren't driven by periods of depression or anxiety. While the heavy workload and stress over the last 11 months have made things much worse, I've had these attention issues my whole life. They are just a constant struggle, regardless of how I'm feeling emotionally.

final_diagnosis.reason: Lifelong, cross-situational pattern of inattentive symptoms beginning in childhood, with clear occupational and home impairment, and without prominent hyperactivity/impulsivity or evidence that symptoms are better explained by mood or anxiety episodes. This is most consistent with ADHD, predominantly inattentive presentation (ICD-10 F90.0).
